purpose.description: Collect adversarial examples where interfaces fail because the environment changes after assumptions have been learned.
purpose.principle: A representation that is sufficient under one regime may become insufficient after the causal structure changes.

formal_condition.interpretation: The interface cannot distinguish states that require different responses because the active regime has changed.

counterexamples.name: Identical observation, different active dynamics
counterexamples.description: The same observed state requires different predictions depending on the hidden regime.

counterexamples.name: Long history preserves outdated assumptions
counterexamples.description: Historical data dominates recent evidence after a regime transition.

counterexamples.name: Fixed model becomes invalid after shift
counterexamples.description: A model trained before the transition continues applying obsolete dynamics.

counterexamples.name: Gradual drift without obvious boundary
counterexamples.description: The environment changes slowly enough that abrupt detectors fail.

counterexamples.name: Stable observations hide changing dynamics
counterexamples.description: Prediction remains accurate temporarily despite incorrect assumptions.

counterexamples.name: Delayed recovery after regime transition
counterexamples.description: The interface eventually adapts but after accumulating prediction errors.

counterexamples.name: Novel regime outside model assumptions
counterexamples.description: The adaptive system tracks known regimes but encounters an unseen one.

counterexamples.name: Insufficient probing fails to reveal change
counterexamples.description: Active exploration exists but perturbations are too weak.

hidden_regime_aliasing.definition: Different causal environments produce the same interface representation.

historical_contamination.definition: Past information reduces accuracy after environmental change.

weak_shift_signal.definition: Change exists but evidence is insufficient.

false_stability.definition: Short-term accuracy hides long-term model failure.

adaptation_delay.definition: The system requires time to update after change.

unmodeled_regime.definition: The environment enters a causal regime outside the representation.

weak_causal_separation.definition: Interventions do not generate enough information to distinguish regimes.

global_summary.central_result: Nonstationary interfaces fail when they preserve state information but discard information about whether the generating process has changed.

decision.meaning: Counterexample suite for nonstationary interface identifiability.

notes: Nonstationary failure is a failure of temporal validity, not merely missing information.
An adaptive system must represent when its own learned mappings stop applying.
The strongest interfaces preserve uncertainty over both state and environment.
